failed_or_abandoned: directdm 2.2.2 WC_5f/WC_4f (RG running classes) crash under numpy 2.5.3 with IndexError in np.delete (out-of-range slice indices, e.g. np.s_[27:144] on a length-131 array, wilson_coefficients.py lines 1551-1556 and 2647-2652). Worked around inside the script by wrapping np.delete to drop out-of-range indices (old numpy behaviour); the installed package was not modified. WC_3f (matching only) works unmodified.

First WimPyDD implementation passed coefficient values as lambda default arguments (c0=..., c1=..., kind=...); WimPyDD treats default arguments as global Hamiltonian parameters shared across coefficients, so pieces overwrote each other (V-A rate collapsed to its O9 admixture, photon dipole N_lo 24.5 instead of 422). Detected by the per-piece diagonal-rate check; fixed with closures; cache deleted and all spectra recomputed.

The full-grid run (87 spectra + final) exceeded the 600 s foreground limit and was moved to the background by the harness; it completed (exit 0). Meanwhile the grid was re-run in resumable foreground chunks (1000 GeV; then 200/4000 GeV restricted to the four compatible structures not yet cached); the final aggregation (--skip-spectra --final) was run on the complete cache, so no reduction of the grid was ultimately needed.
directdm's WilCo_EW class (unbroken-phase running above M_Z) was not used; running is quoted from M_Z down. directdm's NLO coherent tensor corrections (NLO=True) not used.

Anand L identification for L8, L9, L11-L14, L16-L20 could not be established from memory; only class-level statements are made (flagged uncertain), and the anapole = L16 and A-V = L8 hypotheses are rejected by the significance pattern.
wimpydd_generated_files: none (WD.diff_rate used; no response-function files written). Own cache: output/work/P031/cache/*.npz
